title: Merge Better After Toll

source.pdf_page_offset_note: Physical page 1 is the summary sheet; physical page 2 is the contents; physical pages 3-21 carry printed Pages 2-20 after the contents reports Page 1 of 20.

notes: All 21 physical pages were read completely in page-bounded ranges, including summary, contents, every substantive section, references, and the authority letter.
Four contact JPEGs and four focused JPEGs totaled 1,402,778 bytes; every proxy was below 450,000 bytes, only one image was returned per tool call, and no original full-page PNG entered model context.
Focused review reconciled page 9 PCA formulas, pages 11-12 cost/Fourier formulas, pages 13-14 LP formulas and matrix, and page 18 LINGO output.

All 21 rendered PNGs remain on disk for dimensions and coordinates; no blank, clipped, overlapping, missing, or unreadable page was found, and source defects are preserved only as final-pass warnings.

context_sources: The paper cites highway capacity, traffic simulation, design, urban road capacity, prior toll-flow, PCA/AHP, and autonomous-vehicle sources.

No official prompt, native VISSIM file, raw traffic data, Fourier workbook, cost ledger, Mathematica notebook, LINGO model, crash/conflict data, seed ledger, replication output, or field calibration package is bundled with the PDF.

section_map.summary: Input: Post-toll merging creates a design decision over geometry, traffic, safety, and cost. Rhetorical job: Preview the classification, simulation, PCA, optimization, and conditional adjustments in the order used by the paper. Analytical job: Keep each headline result attached to its producing experiment or model rather than collapsing them into one feasibility claim. Output: A selected trapezoid layout, a cost/height optimum, and a transition-matrix recommendation with explicit scenario limits. Handoff: The introduction supplies the toll-plaza mechanism, task decomposition, and assumptions behind the summary.

Input: Toll plazas fan traffic from more booth exits into fewer highway lanes, concentrating queue and conflict pressure. Rhetorical job: Move from public-road pressure through the post-toll mechanism to the four-part problem decomposition. Analytical job: Keep congestion, accidents, cost, throughput, shape, size, and merge pattern as separate analytical inputs. Output: A testable requirement set for a post-toll area rather than a generic traffic-improvement slogan. Handoff: The work overview and assumptions turn those requirements into a closed modeling boundary.

Input: The prompt is recast as design classification, traffic simulation, comprehensive evaluation, and improvement search. Rhetorical job: Use a numbered work map that lets the reader audit whether each requested decision has a downstream artifact. Analytical job: Assign existing-design comparison, simulation, rating, and better-solution search to distinct stages. Output: A requirement-to-method chain from eight design classes through simulation and evaluation to optimization. Handoff: General assumptions bound the resulting chain before parameters are assigned.

Input: A tractable simulation and evaluation requires bounded driver behavior, vehicle class, weather, toll operation, and queue interaction. Rhetorical job: List assumptions as a visible ledger, then preserve their implications for every later result. Analytical job: Distinguish behavioral exclusions from physical operating conditions and from independence assumptions. Output: A conditional evidence domain: cars, normal speed, all-day booths, no modeled accidents from violations, and no queue feedback to booths. Handoff: The design classification and VISSIM configuration instantiate these assumptions.

Input: The post-toll region varies by trapezoid shape, area height/size, and whether lane choices are normal or stipulated. Rhetorical job: Introduce a compact factorial design before simulation so every model label has a geometric and routing meaning. Analytical job: Map shape, size ratio, and merge pattern to eight named cases, preserving the source's abstraction from satellite observations. Output: Eight reproducible design cells: two shapes times two sizes times two merge patterns. Handoff: The simulation model fixes L, B, widths, speed, flow, and detector outputs for all eight cells.

Input: The simulation and cost model use lane, booth, width, speed, time, flow, service, and cost symbols with different units. Rhetorical job: Introduce symbols at the point where a table, parameter calculation, or equation consumes them. Analytical job: Keep simulation quantities (T,L,B,d,D,In,V) separate from cost quantities (C,W1,W2,W3,v,mu,n,C1,C2,F,O,s,k). Output: A typed symbol interface that allows later equations and tables to be checked without guessing units. Handoff: Parameter assignment and optimization consume these symbols and expose where source units remain unclear.

Input: Eight VISSIM cases and the cost model require fixed geometry, flow, toll service, and a fitted influx signal. Rhetorical job: State each value with its source or simplifying choice, then show the conversion that creates a downstream input. Analytical job: Distinguish directly set parameters, cited values, arithmetic derivations, simulated outputs, and a Fourier fit from prior data. Output: A scenario ledger with L=3, B=8, d=3.5 m, D=5.5 m, v=120 km/h, 3600 s, 2400 veh/h ingress, and an eight-term F(t). Handoff: The PCA table and cost equations consume these values with their uncertainty and missing-data boundaries preserved.

Input: The eight classified cases produce throughput, delay, queue length, merge-point count, and height for a multi-index comparison. Rhetorical job: Move from detector design through PCA normalization, correlation, eigenvalue contributions, score, and the size follow-up experiment. Analytical job: Keep simulated values, transformed indices, principal components, and the ranking decision as separate evidence layers. Output: Model 7 receives the highest printed score, while the text also reports a shape interpretation that must be checked against the labels. Handoff: The optimum-solution section consumes the ranking and adds continuous cost and discrete routing models.

Input: Influx, outflux, booth count, height, lane routing, and path length determine the continuous and discrete optimum. Rhetorical job: Trace Fourier demand through waiting integrals and derivatives, then switch to a transition matrix and shortest-path linear program. Analytical job: Retain equation order, variable definitions, objective direction, constraints, and the source's undefined or discrete quantities. Output: B=6 and H=35.6472 m are reported by the cost model; T assigns pairs of tollbooths to three lanes under the path objective. Handoff: The model-testing simulation compares this selected solution with the eight classified cases.

Input: The selected design is tested, then adjusted for light/heavy flow, autonomous vehicles, and booth composition. Rhetorical job: Present each adjustment as a conditional response to a changed demand or vehicle class, keeping the original optimum as the baseline. Analytical job: Separate the model test from claims about traffic regimes, autonomy, and heterogeneous toll service. Output: A scenario-dependent recommendation: close excess booths in light flow, alter routing in heavy flow, and reweight P for booth types. Handoff: Sensitivity analysis examines the transition matrix locally after these modifications.

Input: The simulation table and PCA ranking provide the first empirical comparison of the eight classified designs. Rhetorical job: Report the table, the selected rank, the half-height follow-up, and the mismatch between prose and labels. Analytical job: Keep each number tied to a model, metric, unit, and source table; do not convert the ranking into universal shape superiority. Output: Kind 7 has throughput 2301 veh/h, delay 5.8 s, queue 8.13 m, and 7 merge points; the score table ranks it first at 2.5822. Handoff: The optimum solution expands the score comparison with cost and transition-matrix decisions.

Input: The transition matrix is perturbed with LINGO reduced costs and variable change ranges. Rhetorical job: Describe what the solver reports and which local variables drive the objective without upgrading it to global robustness. Analytical job: Distinguish objective sensitivity for t13/t61 from construction-variable ranges and retain the plotted evidence boundary. Output: The source flags t13 and t61 as costly unit increases and presents a local allowable-error range. Handoff: The weaknesses and independent extensions define the missing global, scenario, and uncertainty checks.

Input: The conclusion inventory claims applicability, a global optimum, flexibility, and technical support, then names data and simulation weaknesses. Rhetorical job: Let the source's self-critique follow the positive summary so limitations remain a final-pass qualification. Analytical job: Separate model adaptability from parameter accuracy, simplifying assumptions, and missing real-world data. Output: A reusable pattern for paired contribution and weakness records, without treating a claimed global optimum as verified. Handoff: The memo and conclusion carry the recommendation into an administrative decision context.

Input: The paper closes by coupling its geometric, optimization, and simulation claims with explicit caveats. Rhetorical job: Synthesize the chain in the same order as the work map, then stop before presenting deployment as established fact. Analytical job: Distinguish what was computed, what was simulated, what was assumed, and what remains unvalidated. Output: A conclusion that is useful for deciding what to test next, not a substitute for field calibration or safety evidence. Handoff: The authority letter restates this conditional decision path for the New Jersey Turnpike Authority.

section_map.section: Letter to New Jersey Turnpike Authority
section_map.summary: Input: The authority letter translates classification, simulation, PCA, cost, LP, traffic, autonomy, and booth-composition findings into advice. Rhetorical job: Use an audience-facing sequence that mirrors the paper's technical chain and then gives conditional operating actions. Analytical job: Keep administrative recommendations tied to their source pages, regimes, and missing validation rather than treating the letter as new data. Output: A staged recommendation: compare existing forms, test the selected cellular design, close excess booths in light flow, divert heavy flow, and re-evaluate adoption. Handoff: The closing asks for overall real-world consideration and leaves construction decisions with the authority.

Input: References, the authority letter, and four-dimensional model graphics preserve provenance and communication context. Rhetorical job: Record external sources and visual artifacts after the substantive argument while keeping them out of the positive model proof. Analytical job: Distinguish cited capacity/autonomy facts, visible matrices and plots, and missing original data or executable files. Output: A provenance and visualization tail that makes the paper auditable without adding unsupported validation. Handoff: The final artifact retains the PDF's 21 physical pages and all visual/table anchors.

assumptions.summary: All motorists obey traffic rules; crashes caused by drink-driving and speeding are excluded from the safety discussion.
Vehicles travel at one average normal-condition speed and weather effects are ignored.
The fleet is treated as 100% cars because other vehicle types are assumed to be a small share.
Queues at downstream merge points do not reduce tollbooth service, excluding spillback across the stage boundary.
All tollbooths operate all day, even though the light-traffic adjustment later proposes closing redundant booths.
Most observed post-toll areas can be represented by right-angled or isosceles trapezoids.
S/H adequately represents area size after booth count, booth width, lane count, and lane width are fixed.
Stipulating left-side vehicles to left lanes and right-side vehicles to right lanes may reduce collision exposure.
Conflict areas in VISSIM adequately represent vehicle collision avoidance at crossed paths.
The number of merge points can stand in for accident-prevention performance, height can stand in for cost, and delay, queue, and throughput can stand in for traffic capacity.
The congestion barrier k depends on downstream lane count L and height H but not on booth count B.
Equal booth service and uniform destination-lane inflow justify uniform P and Q in the base LP.
Autonomous vehicles' computer control and gap adjustment make stipulated merging unnecessary.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The classification crosses shape Sp1/Sp2, size Sz1/Sz2, and merge pattern Mp1/Mp2 to create eight cases.
Small and large size are defined as S/H=1/3 and S/H=1/6.
The VISSIM baseline sets L=3 travel lanes and B=8 tollbooths.
Highway Capacity Manual values are used for d=3.5 m, D=5.5 m, and v=120 km/h.
A cited 12-second booth retention time is converted to approximately 300 vehicles per hour per lane.
Table 1 declares a 3600-second run and total ingress In=2400 veh/h.
Table 2 records height, throughput, delay, average queue length, and merge-point count for all eight designs.
Kind 7 reports H=50.5 m, throughput=2301 veh/h, delay=5.8 s, queue=8.13 m, and seven merge points.
PCA contribution rates are printed as [72.8902,21.8503,3.8901,1.0350,0.3341] percent.
Cumulative contributions are printed as [72.8902,94.7408,98.6309,99.6659,100] percent.
Table 3 ranks model 7 first at 2.5822 and model 2 last at -1.4298.
A half-height follow-up to kind 5 receives -0.6726 versus -0.1332 for kind 5.
The eight-term Fourier influx fit reports omega=2*pi/24=0.2513 and R2=0.9997, but the source dataset is not bundled.
For L=3, the cost model reports B=6 and H=35.6472 m after stationary-point and Hessian reasoning.
The candidate design reports PCA score 4.3026 after simulation and evaluation.
Booth service rates are reported as 5, 7, and 20 for conventional, exact-change, and ETC types, with the time basis not cleanly preserved in the text layer.
The first composition uses booths 1-2 ETC, 3-4 conventional, and 5-6 exact-change; the second uses booths 1-3 ETC, booth 4 conventional, and booths 5-6 exact-change.
Nine references provide external provenance, but no frozen simulation, optimization, fit, or cost input package is supplied.

models.summary: Classify post-toll areas into eight cases from two shapes, two S/H size levels, and two merge patterns.
Simulate the eight design kinds and collect throughput, delay, queue length, merge points, and height for evaluation.
Rank eight simulated designs using cost, traffic, and accident-prevention surrogates.
Convert previously published hourly flow into a minute-level influx signal for the cost model.
Select booth count and trapezoid height by minimizing time, operation, and construction cost.
Allocate booth outflow to downstream lanes while minimizing expected path length.
Insert the selected isosceles, six-booth, stipulated, H=35.6472 m design into VISSIM and score it with the PCA model.
Modify active booths, route restrictions, and outflux weights for traffic level, autonomous vehicles, and booth composition.
Inspect reduced costs and allowable variable ranges around the printed LP optimum.

dependency_graph.handoff: The eight geometry/routing classes define the VISSIM comparison arms.
VISSIM outputs and geometric merge/height values populate the PCA index table.
The size-ranking reversal motivates a continuous height and booth cost model.
Simulation demand context and cited traffic data motivate the fitted influx signal.
F(t) supplies minute-level arrivals to W1 and daily vehicle count n.
Average VISSIM outflux O(t,B) supplies W3.
The merge-pattern result motivates an explicit transition-matrix optimization.
B=6 and H=35.6472 m parameterize the path-allocation LP.
The continuous optimum defines geometry for the candidate test.
The transition matrix defines the stipulated routing for the candidate test.
The baseline candidate is modified under traffic, autonomy, and booth-composition scenarios.
The base LP solution is passed to LINGO's local sensitivity report.
Composition-adjusted matrices reveal which route variables require local sensitivity attention.

verification.summary: The complete text and rendered-page pass confirms the two shapes, two S/H levels, and two merge patterns used to form eight cases.
The visual pass confirms the page says H=50.25 m for both small and large areas even though S/H=1/6 would imply about 100.5 m; Table 2 later uses 105 m.
Table 1 and Figures 2-10 visually confirm the declared parameters, conflict areas, and all eight design networks.
Table 2 was reconciled across all rows and five columns rather than reading only the winning design.
The focused PCA proxy confirms Equations (1)-(6), the contribution vectors, three-component retention, and source notation defects.
Table 3 confirms model 7 is rank 1; Figures 7-10 establish that model 7 is isosceles, contrary to the prose statement favoring right-angled trapezoids.
The cost-model focus proxy confirms Table 4 and Equation (7), including the repeated cos(t omega) term and time-unit ambiguity.
The cost focus confirms Equations (8)-(12), B=6, and H=35.6472 m while preserving malformed limits and the continuous treatment of discrete B.
The LP focus confirms Equations (13)-(15), Figure 11, uniform P/Q, and undefined SD.
The LP focus confirms Equation (16), the base transition matrix, paired-booth lane assignment, and the candidate score 4.3026.
Figure 12 confirms only that a candidate network was represented in VISSIM; no independent field or held-out validation is shown.
The first composition matrix and service-rate prose were visually checked; its fractional entries do not support a simple one-lane-only reading without an explicit decision rule.
The second composition matrix and the repeated lane interpretation were retained rather than silently harmonized.
The focused LINGO proxy confirms Figures 13-14 are solver tables/screenshots, not global robustness or construction-tolerance experiments.
The source's own weaknesses corroborate parameter-provenance, simplifying-assumption, and missing-real-data limitations.

results_trace.summary: Stipulated designs 3, 4, 7, and 8 use seven merge points versus 24 for normal designs 1, 2, 5, and 6.
Kind 7 has the highest throughput, lowest delay, and shortest queue among the eight printed cases.
The first PCA component is interpreted as throughput-dominant, the second as cost-dominant, and the third as accident-prevention-dominant.
Table 3 ranks kind 7 first at 2.5822 and kind 3 second at 1.6134.
The half-height experiment supports a local non-monotone height hypothesis but does not identify a continuous optimum by itself.
The cost model reports the stationary design B=6 and H=35.6472 m for L=3.
The base LP assigns booths 1-2 to lane 1, booths 3-4 to lane 2, and booths 5-6 to lane 3.
The selected isosceles, six-booth, stipulated design receives score 4.3026, higher than the eight baseline scores.
For light flow the paper recommends closing redundant booths to reduce operating cost, conditional on unchanged throughput.
For heavy flow it proposes restricting distant booth-to-lane assignments, while admitting possible queue growth.
The autonomous-vehicle section proposes removing merge restrictions based on cited safety and efficiency characteristics.
Composition-adjusted LP runs produce T1 and T2 and are interpreted as routing booths 1, 2-3, and 4-6 toward lanes 1, 2, and 3.
LINGO reduced costs flag t13 and t61 as undesirable long-path assignment increases.
LINGO allowable ranges are presented as a reasonable construction-error range, though that interpretation is unvalidated.

contributions.summary: The summary presents a complete pipeline from observed designs to simulation, PCA, continuous cost optimization, discrete route allocation, scenario adjustment, and sensitivity.
The introduction explains the fan-in mechanism before introducing preferred geometry or methods.
The four-part task map assigns baseline analysis, simulation, evaluation, and improvement to distinct sections.
The three-factor taxonomy makes the eight comparison cases reproducible at the conceptual level.
The simulation section declares detectors and queue counters before using their outputs in PCA.
The evaluation model separates safety, cost, and traffic proxies instead of hiding them in a single unexplained score.
Contribution and cumulative-contribution vectors explain why three components are retained.
A failed monotonic size assumption is followed by a targeted half-height experiment, creating a useful hypothesis-to-test loop.
The total-cost definition expands construction cost to include traveler time and booth operations.
The cost model exposes W1, W2, and W3 before differentiation, making the intended mechanism inspectable despite formula defects.
The transition matrix converts merge-pattern prose into an explicit booth-to-lane allocation interface.
The selected design is returned to the simulation and PCA layers instead of being accepted directly from optimization.
Light and heavy traffic are treated as different operating regimes with different control actions.
Heterogeneous booth service is incorporated by modifying P rather than pretending all booths remain identical.
Reduced costs and allowable ranges give the LP a local post-optimality check, even though broader robustness is missing.
The authority letter mirrors the technical chain and translates it into audience-specific actions.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The complete method preview may reduce coverage-check cost for a judge; this is a class-J hypothesis, not scoring evidence.
A full eight-row metric table may make trade-offs easier to audit; this remains a class-J hypothesis.
Returning the optimized candidate to simulation and PCA may strengthen closure; this is not observed judge preference.
A decision-maker letter may support task closure by translating results into actions; it is not empirical scoring evidence.

weaknesses.summary: The text gives H=50.25 m for both S/H=1/3 and 1/6; the latter implies about 100.5 m, while Table 2 uses 105 m.
Merge-point count is an unvalidated surrogate for accident prevention and omits crossing angle, speed, exposure, and conflict severity.
The printed standard-deviation expression appears to subtract mu_i rather than the column mean mu_j.
Reciprocal transformations, percentage units, eigenvectors, normalized table, and score precision lack a reproducible ledger.
Model 7 is isosceles according to Figures 7-10, but the prose says right-angled trapezoids are better.
Equation (7) repeats cos(t omega) where a fifth harmonic may be intended, and minutes versus a 24-hour omega are not reconciled.
The W1 double integral has malformed limits and mixed variables, so its units and queue accumulation are unclear.
W3 repeats the unclear integral construction and relies on unarchived O(t,B) and k values.
Booth count B is integer, yet the method differentiates and reports a stationary point without integer-neighborhood enumeration.
The path-length formula contains undefined SD and no verified geometric coordinate convention.
Nonnegativity, probability bounds, complete row/column constraints, and a proof that path length represents throughput are absent.
VISSIM version, files, route rules, detector boundaries, warm-up, seeds, replications, calibration, uncertainty, and raw outputs are missing.
Autonomous-vehicle claims are used to remove merge restrictions without a controlled mixed-fleet safety or capacity experiment.
Reduced costs and allowable ranges test a local LP basis only; they do not establish global model, simulation, demand, or construction robustness.
Reported digits such as H=35.6472 and score=4.3026 exceed the identification strength of cited, simulated, and incompletely archived inputs.
